ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A person in your family who lived long before your grandparents is an (1 mark)
   A. orphan
   B. widow
   C. ancestor
   D. elder

2. Which sentence is wrong? (1 mark)
   A. I have books.
   B. I have the book.
   C. I have a book.
   D. I have an books.

3. The word 'the' is said as 'thee' before (1 mark)
   A. a plural only
   B. a name
   C. a vowel sound
   D. a consonant sound

4. Which is written in block letters? (1 mark)
   A. wanjiku kamau, in small letters
   B. Wanjiku Kamau, with capitals at the start of each name
   C. Wanjiku, in joined writing
   D. WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only

5. If you make a small mistake on a form, you should (1 mark)
   A. tear the page
   B. scribble over it
   C. leave it
   D. draw one neat line through it and write the correct word

6. A simile compares two things using (1 mark)
   A. who or which
   B. if or then
   C. but or and
   D. like or as

7. In a plan for a story, the middle usually tells (1 mark)
   A. what happens
   B. the last sentence
   C. only the title
   D. the name of the school

8. 'The sun was as warm as a fresh loaf of bread.' This sentence uses (1 mark)
   A. a command
   B. a question
   C. a list
   D. a simile

9. Which word has the vowel /e/? (1 mark)
   A. late
   B. bed
   C. pain
   D. day

10. Which pair is a minimal pair for /e/ and /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. pat, bat
   B. ten, den
   C. let, late
   D. pin, bin

11. To scan a text means to (1 mark)
   A. draw pictures
   B. read every word slowly
   C. copy the text
   D. look quickly for one fact

12. Which letter is silent in 'write'? (1 mark)
   A. r
   B. w
   C. i
   D. t

13. On most maps, north is at the (1 mark)
   A. right
   B. left
   C. top
   D. bottom

14. Pronouns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. The house is ours'.
   B. The house is ours's.
   C. The house is ours.
   D. The house is our's.

15. The short form of 'I would' is (1 mark)
   A. I've
   B. I'll
   C. I'm
   D. I'd

16. A story that you heard on the radio and write in your own words is (1 mark)
   A. a map
   B. a menu
   C. a receipt
   D. a retelling

17. In the noun 'INcrease', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. the last letter
   B. the first syllable
   C. the second syllable
   D. no syllable

18. Which question ends with a rising voice? (1 mark)
   A. Did you save the file?
   B. Who saved the file?
   C. When did you save the file?
   D. How did you save it?

19. What must every sentence begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A capital letter
   B. A question mark
   C. A full stop
   D. A comma

20. Which tense is best for telling the story? (1 mark)
   A. a new tense in each line
   B. past tense
   C. future tense only
   D. no tense

21. Which of these tells you what a book is about before you read it? (1 mark)
   A. The back cover summary
   B. The page numbers
   C. The price sticker
   D. The printer's name

22. What does the proverb 'Look before you leap' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Jump as high as you can
   B. Always look at your feet
   C. Think carefully before you act
   D. Do not go outside

23. Which word begins with the sound /ʧ/? (1 mark)
   A. sun
   B. sack
   C. soil
   D. chicken

24. Which sentence has a comma before 'but' joining two full sentences? (1 mark)
   A. I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   B. I was tired but I finished sweeping,
   C. I was tired but, I finished sweeping.
   D. I was, tired but I finished sweeping.

25. What is a descriptive composition? (1 mark)
   A. A letter to a friend
   B. A list of numbers
   C. Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity
   D. A story with a problem to solve

26. Which word begins with the voiced sound /ð/? (1 mark)
   A. think
   B. three
   C. this
   D. thumb

27. What does it mean to read a poem interpretively? (1 mark)
   A. To count the words
   B. To read it silently in one second
   C. To copy it
   D. To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice

28. In a comic, what do speech bubbles show? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. The author's name
   C. What the characters say
   D. The price

29. Which is a sentence in the future tense about tomorrow? (1 mark)
   A. Yesterday I visited my grandmother.
   B. I was visiting her.
   C. I visit my grandmother now.
   D. Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.

30. Which is the correct spelling of the word that tells where you live? (1 mark)
   A. address
   B. adres
   C. addres
   D. adress

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write a short talk of four sentences on how to care for a sick friend. (4 marks)

32. Give a memory trick for spelling 'necessary' or 'separate'. (2 marks)

33. Write a or an before each word: egg, banana, umbrella, hour. (2 marks)

34. Write four descriptive sentences about your classroom. (4 marks)

35. Name the seven coordinating conjunctions. (3 marks)

36. Explain how guide words help you find a word quickly. (3 marks)

37. Give the meaning of each word and use it in a sentence: (a) harvest (b) fertilizer. (4 marks)

38. List three steps to follow before writing a pictorial composition. (3 marks)

39. Write four sentences about your family. Use a, an and the at least once. (4 marks)

40. Plan a composition called 'My School Compound' by saying what goes into each of three paragraphs. (3 marks)

41. Write the short forms of: did not, she has, we will, let us. (4 marks)

42. Write a friendly letter of about five sentences to a friend in another school about new road safety words you learnt. (5 marks)

43. Explain what word stress is. Give one example. (2 marks)

44. Write four sentences about your morning: two with have or has and two with had. (4 marks)

45. Give three strategies that help you read more fluently. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — ancestor
   Ancestors are family members from long ago.

2. D — I have an books.
   A and an cannot be used before a plural noun.

3. C — a vowel sound
   We say thee egg and thuh boy.

4. D — WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   Block letters are capital letters.

5. D — draw one neat line through it and write the correct word
   A neat single line keeps the form readable.

6. D — like or as
   A simile uses like or as, for example as brave as a lion.

7. A — what happens
   The middle tells the events, including any problem.

8. D — a simile
   It compares the sun to bread using as ... as.

9. B — bed
   Bed has the short vowel /e/.

10. C — let, late
   Let and late differ in the vowel sound.

11. D — look quickly for one fact
   Scanning is used to find a name, number or word.

12. B — w
   We say rite, so the w is silent.

13. C — top
   North is shown at the top of a map.

14. C — The house is ours.
   Possessive pronouns are written without an apostrophe.

15. D — I'd
   I would can be shortened to I'd.

16. D — a retelling
   You tell the same story in new words.

17. B — the first syllable
   The noun is IN-crease and the verb is in-CREASE.

18. A — Did you save the file?
   It is a yes or no question.

19. A — A capital letter
   Capital letters start sentences.

20. B — past tense
   Stories are usually told in the past tense.

21. A — The back cover summary
   The back cover gives a short summary.

22. C — Think carefully before you act
   It advises us to think before we do something.

23. D — chicken
   'Chicken' begins with 'ch', said /ʧ/.

24. A — I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

25. C — Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity
   It describes so that the reader can imagine.

26. C — this
   'This' has the voiced 'th'.

27. D — To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   Interpretive reading brings out meaning and feeling.

28. C — What the characters say
   Speech bubbles hold spoken words.

29. D — Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.
   'Will visit' shows the future.

30. A — address
   Address has a double d and a double s.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two caring actions such as visiting and listening, and a closing thank-you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the four parts.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: 'Necessary' has one collar (c) and two sleeves (ss); 'separate' has 'a rat' in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trick and 1 for a correct explanation.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: an egg, a banana, an umbrella, an hour
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct answer.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct descriptive sentences with capitals and full stops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all seven, 2 for five or six, 1 for three or four.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Guide words show the first and last word on a page. If your word comes between them alphabetically, it is on that page. If not, turn forward or backward.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what guide words show, 1 mark for comparing your word, 1 mark for turning pages.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) Harvest: to gather crops that are ready. We harvest maize in August. (b) Fertilizer: something added to soil to help plants grow. The farmer put fertilizer on the field.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each word: 1 for the meaning and 1 for a correct sentence.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at all the pictures, put them in order, ask who, where and what, make notes, think of a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have a brother. He has an old bicycle. The bicycle is red. We ride it in the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence that uses the articles correctly.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Paragraph 1: what the compound is and where. Paragraph 2: details such as trees, playground, buildings. Paragraph 3: how I feel about it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each paragraph.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: didn't, she's, we'll, let's
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: A letter with address and date, Dear ..., a body that mentions words such as roundabout, foot bridge and railway crossing, a closing and a name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 for greeting, 1 for body content, 1 for closing and name, 1 for punctuation.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Word stress is the syllable we say more strongly in a word, for example the first syllable in HOS-pi-tal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have brushed my teeth. She has swept the floor. We had eaten before we left. He had washed before school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Preview the text; read in phrases; follow the punctuation; re-read; read along with a model.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
